title: About me
text:
Brenda Anague is currently PhD student in Applied Mathematics, at the Department of Mathematics, at the university of KwaZulu-Natal in South Africa. Her PhD is funded by Deepmind Technologies Limited through the African Institute for Mathematical Sciences Research and Innovation Centre (AIMS RIC) in Rwanda. More earlier, she completed a Bachelor in Mathematics and Computer Science in 2019, and a Master in Applied Mathematics in 2021 from the University of Dschang in Cameroon. In additon, she later graduated in 2022 with a second master in Mathematical Science from the African Institute for Mathecatical Sciences (AIMS) Cameroon.
She is currently working at the intersection of partial differential equations and scientific computing with a particular focus on developing robust computation methods for solving source inversion problems of PDEs using PINNs, as well as conducting theoretical convergence analysis of PINNs for approximating PDEs solutions.

title: Brenda Anague
text:
Research

Physics-Informed Neural Networks
My research investigates physics-informed neural networks for source and parameter estimation in parabolic PDEs, including the use of adaptive training strategies such as Neural Tangent Kernel. In addtion, I also investigate the use of conditional stability based on Carlemann estimate for source inversion problems to estimate theoretically the approximation error of PINNs in source inversion problems.


PDE Discovery
I investigate data-driven approaches for discovering governing equations and initial conditions from sparse and noisy observations of solutions of parabolic PDES, including Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy).


Convergence Analysis of PINNs
I study the estimation of the theoretical convergence rate of PINNs in solving parabolic PDEs, under Barron regularity assumptions.

title: Brenda Anague
text:
Current Research Focus


Inverse problems with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
My research investigates on how to develop robust data-driven methods such as Physics-informed Neural Networks for source and parameter estimation in parabolic PDEs, including adaptive training strategies such as the Neural Tangent Kernel. In addition, I also estimate the approximation error bound of PINNs in solving source inversion problems from conditional stability based on Carlemann estimate.


Discovering governing equations and initial condition of parabolic PDEs from sparse and noisy data
I develop data-driven approaches that combine Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) with PINNs, to discover governing equations recover and the associated initial conditions from sparse and noisy observations of solutions of parabolic PDEs.


Convergence analysis of PINNs in parabolic PDE
I study the convergence rates of PINNs in approximating parabolic PDEs under spectral Barron space regularity assumptions.

About
I am currently a PhD student in Applied Mathematics in the Discipline of Mathemtics of the School of Agriculture and Science
at the University of KwaZulu Natal. My research is funded by DeepMind Technologies Limited through the African Institute for Mathematical Sciences Research and Innovation Centre (AIMS RIC) in Rwanda.
From 2019 to 2021, I hold my first Master’s degree in Applied Mathematics from the University of Dschang (Cameroon), and from September 2021 to June 2022, I completed a second Master’s degree in Mathematical Sciences through a Scolarship at the African Institute for Mathematical Science Cameroon.
My current research work combines partial differential equations, inverse problems, numerical analysis and and scientific computing. with a particular focus on builing robust computational methods for solving source inversion problems of PDEs using Physis-informed Neural Networks (PINNs), as well as their theoretical convergence analysis in approximating PDE solutions.

title: Research
text:
Research Details

Convergence analysis of PINNs for parabolic PDEs under spectral Barron regularities
This project studies the theoretical convergence of physics-informed neural networks for parabolic partial differential equations under regularity assumptions formulated in spectral Barron spaces.
The aim is to establish rigorous approximation and convergence results connecting the neural-network approximation, discretization, and PDE solution.
Back to research projects



Equation learning for parabolic PDEs from sparse data
This project investigates the recovery of governing equations for parabolic PDEs from sparse observations.
The approach combines physics-informed neural networks with sparse regression to identify the governing equation, source function, and initial condition.
Back to research projects



Source and parameter estimation for parabolic PDEs using PINNs
This project focuses on the inverse problem of estimating unknown source functions and PDE parameters from sparse and noisy observations.
The work combines physics-informed neural networks with adaptive training strategies and includes theoretical analysis of approximation errors.
Back to research projects



Retrieval of biological and chemical crop traits using PINNs
This project investigated the use of physics-informed neural networks for retrieving biological and chemical crop traits from hyperspectral and multispectral data.
Back to research projects



The study of over-parameterization for physics-informed neural networks
This MSc research investigated the training dynamics of physics-informed neural networks in the over-parameterized regime.
Back to research projects



Valuation and hedging of options in discrete markets
This project studied investment strategies for hedging financial risk using the Cox–Ross–Rubinstein model and connections with stochastic differential equations such as the Black–Scholes model.
Back to research projects



Finite element methods for elliptic problems and simulation
Project on finite element methods for elliptic boundary value problems and numerical simulation.
Back to research projects



The Hamilton–Jacobi equation
Project studying the Hamilton–Jacobi equation as part of advanced work in partial differential equations.
Back to research projects



Sobolev spaces and variational formulations
Project on Sobolev spaces and the variational formulation of elliptic boundary value problems in N dimensions.
Back to research projects



Use of kinetic theory to build a biological model
BSc thesis investigating the use of kinetic theory to construct a biological model.
